speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a rash on your scalp and forehead; how long have you had these symptoms, and have they been accompanied by fever or joint pain? To help narrow this down, I will need to see the specific appearance of the lesions. REQUEST IMAGES: Scalp and forehead rash photos.

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the seasonal flare-up and paternal history strongly suggest an inflammatory condition. To confirm if this is psoriasis or a related disorder like seborrheic dermatitis, have you noticed any thick silvery scales or hair loss on the scalp? REQUEST TEST: TSH, Vitamin D, Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR)

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal inflammatory markers and lack of systemic symptoms, are there areas of the rash that seem to itch intensely or bleed when scratched? Additionally, does the scalp rash appear to be thick and silvery, or is it more greasy and yellowish?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (cradle cap) with seasonal exacerbation. The presence of greasy, yellowish scales rather than silvery ones, combined with a family history of psoriasis, strongly points to this common inflammatory condition. While the father has psoriasis, your baby's symptoms are classic for seborrheic dermatitis, which is often triggered by temperature changes. No further tests are needed at this time; treatment typically involves gentle emollients and mild antifungal shampoos.
